contexts.api_surface: GET /v1/alerts, POST /v1/alerts/:id/ack, POST /v1/alerts/:id/resolution, GET/PUT /v1/projects/:id/alert-channels, POST /v1/alert-channels/:id/test
contexts.description: Implements the multi-channel alerting subsystem: detects breach conditions (budget, margin, relay unroutable), composes alert payloads, routes them to webhook or ntfy channels with per-project overrides, tracks breach attribution across time windows, and maintains the alert ledger with acknowledge and resolution flows. The canary module watches per-prompt variant metrics and fires alerts on quality regressions. Rejection counts are periodically flushed from in-process RAM into durable alert rows.
contexts.name: alerts-system

contexts.api_surface: Generates /openapi.json; provides MCP tool catalog; drives CLI verb tree
contexts.description: The type system and surface-generation machinery for the LightTrack HTTP API contract. Defines the core vocabulary (Endpoint, Param, McpTool, Method, Access, TypeRef) that every endpoint row is written in, plus the DSL helpers, nested-route utilities, and the renderers that convert the single endpoint table into an OpenAPI document and an MCP tool catalog. Everything downstream — the axum router, the CLI, the MCP server — is held to this table by bijection tests.
contexts.name: api-contract-core

contexts.api_surface: Declares all /v1/* routes with their HTTP methods, auth scopes, parameters, and multi-surface coverage
contexts.description: The canonical list of every LightTrack HTTP endpoint, split into domain modules that mirror the axum router order. Each module declares a static ENDPOINTS slice using the contract DSL, recording the method, path, parameters, access rule, MCP tool coverage, CLI verb path, and render kind for each route. This table is the single source of truth that the router bijection test, the MCP server, and the CLI are all held to.
contexts.name: api-endpoint-table

contexts.description: End-to-end integration test suite for the API, wiring the full axum Router via tower `oneshot` calls against in-process SQLite. Covers auth throttling, collective federation, dataset lineage, forecast projections, ingest flows, label management, limit scoping, margin policies, prompt gating, redaction, relay workflows, rollup queries, schedule execution, storage accounting, multi-tenancy isolation, trace ingestion, unpriced cost detection, and judge-verdict identity. Each test module targets a specific domain handler path.
contexts.name: api-integration-tests

contexts.api_surface: GET /health, GET /health/live, GET /health/ready, GET /openapi.json, GET /v1/capabilities, POST/GET /v1/projects, PUT/DELETE /v1/projects/:id, POST/GET /v1/projects/:id/keys
contexts.description: Core API wiring: router construction, shared application state, authentication (dev/enforced mode, admin key, per-project API keys), auth-failure throttling, credential boundary boot check, request guards, health endpoints, OpenAPI document generation, HTTP client, idempotency for billing webhooks, request logging, project and key management, and schema registry. This is the entry point and the glue that all domain handlers plug into.
contexts.name: api-platform

contexts.api_surface: POST /billing/webhook/{provider} (consumed by API crate; this crate is a library)
contexts.description: Verifies signed webhooks from Stripe and Polar and normalizes them into canonical RevenueEvent records for profit and margin tracking. Each provider adapter implements a framework-agnostic BillingSource trait that accepts raw request bytes and headers, performs HMAC-based signature verification with replay-tolerance, and maps paid/refunded events to a shared revenue schema. Currency amounts are converted to USD through a config-seeded FxTable that handles per-currency decimal places (zero-decimal JPY, three-decimal KWD, etc.) and flags unconverted currencies rather than silently applying a 1:1 fallback.
contexts.name: billing-provider-adapters

contexts.api_surface: run_claude, probe, resolve_claude_bin, run_exec (library API)
contexts.description: The single seam for all headless-Claude subprocess spawning: `invocation/` enforces posture rules (mode → argv shape, cwd policy, tool allowlist, auth policy) before any child is spawned, so contradictions become errors rather than wasted paid calls. `codex/` adapts the Codex CLI (`codex exec`) for GPT models behind a ChatGPT seat, applying the same posture and audit model. `sandbox/` wraps Docker and Contree isolation runtimes for `exec` rubric dimensions that run untrusted candidate code, exposing a `SandboxRunner` trait behind an `Arc<dyn _>` on `EngineConfig`.
contexts.name: claude-invocation-and-execution

contexts.api_surface: lt costs, lt rollup, lt forecast, lt margin, lt revenue, lt prices, lt prompts, lt rubrics, lt labels, lt datasets, lt use-cases, lt collective, lt relay, lt events, lt traces
contexts.description: Implements the `lt` CLI subcommands for all observability, evaluation, and intelligence domains: cost/event/trace/rollup/forecast queries, margin and revenue reporting, price-book inspection, prompt registry queries, rubric/label/dataset/use-case management, collective model leaderboard, and the device relay fleet. Each domain module pairs a `cli/` arg-definition file with a sibling handler module that calls the HTTP client and renders the response.
contexts.name: cli-domain-commands

contexts.api_surface: lt health, lt capabilities, lt projects, lt keys, lt limits, lt alerts, lt schedules, lt jobs
contexts.description: Implements the `lt` operator CLI's core plumbing and management subcommands: argument parsing (clap), the blocking HTTP client, query-string building, and the commands that manage projects, API keys, usage limits, alert rules, alert delivery channels, and recurring schedules/jobs. A developer reads `main.rs` to see the full verb dispatch, `cli/mod.rs` for the clap enum tree, and `http.rs` for how every domain module talks to the API.
contexts.name: cli-infrastructure

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/collective/digest, GET /api/collective/leaderboard, POST /api/collective/contribute
contexts.description: Implements the federated benchmark-sharing data model: digest building and versioning, leaderboard merging, model alias resolution, contribution privacy controls, rigor classification, coverage spread computation, and contribution record lifecycle. These types power the collective digest protocol by which multiple operators share anonymized benchmark results without exposing raw traces.
contexts.name: collective-intelligence-types

contexts.api_surface: GET /v1/collective/digest, POST /v1/collective/ingest, GET /v1/collective/leaderboard, POST /v1/collective/contribute, GET /v1/collective/contributions, DELETE /v1/collective/contribution
contexts.description: Implements a privacy-safe federated model leaderboard where instances can share anonymised benchmark digests with a hub and receive merged real-world performance data in return. Handles digest construction (k-anonymity enforced), contribution ledger, hub-side ingestion and sanitisation, leaderboard merging, and withdraw/withdraw-all flows. The auto-contribute module fires on a schedule to push updates without manual admin action.
contexts.name: collective-leaderboard

contexts.api_surface: Wire types consumed by POST /api/events, GET /api/traces, GET /api/rollup
contexts.description: Defines the normalized wire types that every LightTrack crate shares: the LlmEvent ingest record, Trace/Span tree, rollup query/row shapes, project API-key and redaction model, provider/model canonicalization, prompt versioning, and relay task lifecycle. These pure data types are I/O-free; all other crates depend on this module to avoid payload drift between the API and the Rust client SDK.
contexts.name: core-observability-types

contexts.api_surface: POST/GET /v1/projects/:id/limits, GET /v1/limits/status, GET /v1/limits/usage, GET /v1/forecast, GET /v1/margin, POST /v1/revenue, PUT /v1/prices/:provider/:model, POST /v1/billing/:provider/webhook
contexts.description: Controls LLM spend governance (per-project caps, usage rollups by scope, margin guardrails) and revenue tracking (billing webhooks, model prices, revenue recording, margin simulation and trend analysis). Forecast module projects future spend and margin erosion and emits pre-emptive alerts. Bridges operator-facing revenue data with LLM cost rollups to produce net-margin views by customer or product.
contexts.name: cost-and-revenue-governance

contexts.api_surface: POST/GET /v1/relay/tasks, POST /v1/relay/lease, POST /v1/relay/tasks/:id/result, POST /v1/relay/tasks/:id/renew, POST/GET /v1/relay/devices, DELETE /v1/relay/devices/:id, GET /v1/relay/actions
contexts.description: Provides a task relay system for dispatching work to enrolled edge devices (e.g. running Claude CLI locally). Devices lease queued tasks, heartbeat progress, and report results; the API side enqueues tasks, polls status, and records the action fingerprint ledger. Includes device enrolment/revocation, fenced lease renewal, unroutable-task alerting, and a snapshot route that promotes relay run outputs into evaluation datasets.
contexts.name: device-relay

contexts.api_surface: POST /api/relay/lease (consumes), POST /api/relay/settle (consumes), POST /api/relay/renew (consumes), configurable per-action HTTP connector (produces)
contexts.description: Implements the `lt-agent` binary — the device-side half of the relay protocol. It polls one or more cloud LightTrack sources over outbound HTTPS, leases due tasks filtered by its local action inventory, executes each with the local Claude Code CLI, delivers results via per-action HTTP connectors, and settles every task back to the originating cloud with a fenced heartbeat that detects lease takeovers mid-run. The agent is entirely pull-based so it runs behind a NAT with no inbound ports; all credentials stay on the device.
contexts.name: device-relay-agent

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/prices, GET /api/margin, GET /api/forecast, GET /api/cost-summary
contexts.description: Implements LightTrack's cost and revenue model: the PriceBook that maps model tokens to dollar cost, margin computation across dimensions, policy-triggered actions when margin drops, simulation of assumptions, trend series, budget forecasting, revenue event tracking, and unpriced-model ledgering. Together these types answer 'is this deployment profitable?' and drive automated cost controls.
contexts.name: economics-margin-pricing

contexts.api_surface: POST/GET /v1/projects/:id/benchmarks, GET /v1/benchmarks/:id/gate, POST /v1/scores, GET /v1/scores, POST/GET /v1/labels, GET /v1/judges/trust, POST/GET /v1/datasets/:id/items, POST/GET /v1/projects/:id/prompts, POST /v1/projects/:id/prompts/:name/promote
contexts.description: Manages the full LLM quality evaluation pipeline: datasets (create, freeze, fork, import), scoring and labels, rubrics, judge trust, human calibration, prompt registry with versioning and canary promotion, and benchmark runs with CI gate verdicts. Implements a regression-gated promote flow where a prompt version must pass its linked benchmark before a label can advance to production. Depends on the job queue for async benchmark execution.
contexts.name: evaluation-pipeline

contexts.api_surface: render(kind, value) -> Option<String> — kinds: list_benchmarks, get_benchmark, get_benchmark_runs, check_benchmark_gate, list_jobs, list_schedules, get_job, list_datasets, get_dataset, list_dataset_items, list_rubrics, get_rubric, list_prompts, get_prompt, get_prompt_quality, compare, get_margin, list_margin_policies, get_limit_status, list_limits, list_prices, list_price_history, list_unpriced_models
contexts.description: Renders evaluation, governance, and pricing API responses into Markdown tables for the `lt` CLI and `lt-mcp` server. Covers benchmark listings and detail/gate views, job and schedule lists, dataset and item tables, rubric and prompt detail, prompt-quality tables, compare leaderboards, effort-curve views, usage-limit status, margin reports and simulations, margin-policy lists, price books, and unpriced-model ledgers. Shares the `lighttrack-render` crate's dispatch table and `md` helper; the integration tests in `tests/render.rs` verify two-directional bijection between this crate and `lighttrack-contract`.
contexts.name: evaluation-rendering

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/benchmarks, POST /api/benchmarks/run, GET /api/scores, GET /api/rubrics, GET /api/datasets
contexts.description: Defines the full evaluation pipeline data model: datasets and lineage, rubrics and dimension checks, benchmark runs and judge verdicts, calibration items and trust scores, use-case registry, grounding claim verification, job scheduling and lease fencing for async benchmark execution, and benchmark target resolution. These types are shared by the engine, runner, and store crates that execute and persist evaluation results.
contexts.name: evaluation-scoring-types

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/events, POST /v1/events/batch, POST /v1/traces (OTLP), GET /v1/events, GET /v1/events/:id, GET /v1/traces, GET /v1/traces/:id, GET /v1/costs, GET /v1/usecases, GET /v1/rollup, GET /v1/ingest/status
contexts.description: Handles ingestion and querying of LLM call events, the core telemetry pipeline. Single-event POST, batch ingest, OTLP/OpenTelemetry trace import, and keyset-paginated query with cost, rollup, trace, and use-case views. Enforces body limits, load-shedding admission, timestamp skew, and ingest proximity checks; connects to the store for durable event persistence.
contexts.name: event-ingest

contexts.api_surface: Implements lighttrack_store::Store; connects via firestore://<project-id> URL
contexts.description: Implements the LightTrack `Store` trait over the Firestore REST API for the core observability and governance data plane: LLM event ingestion, cost aggregation, rollup/forecast, project and API-key management, usage limits, margin policies, pricing, prompt registry, and revenue tracking. Uses blocking `reqwest` with rustls; auth via emulator or `GOOGLE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. The `rest` and `codec` modules form the HTTP transport and Firestore document serialization layer that all domain modules share.
contexts.name: firestore-core-dataplane

contexts.api_surface: Implements Store benchmark/dataset/rubric/job/label/collective/alert surfaces; conformance suite via Firestore emulator
contexts.description: Implements the Store trait's evaluation, benchmarking, collective intelligence, and alerting surfaces over Firestore REST. Covers benchmark definitions and runs, dataset/item management, rubric storage, async job leases, human verdict labels with calibration history, collective leaderboard entries and contributor ledger, and the alert ledger with dedup, delivery tracking, and routing channels. The conformance test suite asserts correct `Unsupported` refusals (e.g. traces) and surface-level parity against the backend capability manifest.
contexts.name: firestore-eval-collective

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/chat/completions (OpenAI-compatible); GET /v1/limits/status (consumed from LightTrack API for admission); POST /v1/events/batch (emitted to LightTrack API for telemetry)
contexts.description: Provides a single loopback OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint (`lt-gateway`) that apps point their OpenAI SDK at, resolving a use-case route name or literal `provider/model` to an ordered chain of seat-metered CLI backends (claude -p, codex exec, or HTTP providers). It walks the chain on failure, classifying each error as exhausted/transient/terminal, holding spent seats out via a cooldown timer, and gate-checking the project's usage limits via the LightTrack admission API before any seat is spent. Every attempt — success or failure — is recorded as a structured event to the LightTrack API with shared trace IDs so failover appears as one story in the trace view.
contexts.name: gateway-proxy

contexts.api_surface: run_judge, run_rubric_judge, run_rubric_judge_with_evidence, run_pairwise, run_rubric_batch (library API)
contexts.description: Implements LLM-as-judge scoring for benchmark runs: executes rubric dimensions (LLM, grounding, deterministic), batches judge calls, computes weighted overall scores with per-dimension floors, and detects prompt-injection attempts via nonce fencing. Prompt builders in `prompts/` assemble the judge/eval/rubric/pairwise schemas; `scorers/` handles non-LLM dimensions (exact, regex, numeric, json_valid, contains); `parse` does JSON extraction with one-shot repair re-ask; `pairwise` drives head-to-head comparisons. Outputs `RubricOutcome` / `JudgeOutcome` / `PairwiseOutcome` consumed by the runner and API layers.
contexts.name: judge-and-scoring

contexts.api_surface: MCP stdio JSON-RPC 2.0: tools/list, tools/call, prompts/list, prompts/get, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read; proxies to LIGHTTRACK_URL REST API
contexts.description: The `lt-mcp` binary implements a Model Context Protocol server that exposes LightTrack's full observability, benchmarking, and governance data to Claude Code and AI agents via stdio JSON-RPC 2.0. It is a thin, stateless HTTP client of the LightTrack API — it never touches the database directly, so a misbehaving tool call can at worst produce a 4xx and cannot corrupt state. The server dispatches 50+ read/write tools across four sub-catalogs (core reads, prompt-registry tools, relay inspection, and gated writes), exposes `lighttrack://` resource URI templates for attaching traces/events/benchmarks, and serves seven pre-built slash-command prompts (cost-report, limit-check, benchmark-leaderboard, etc.); the tool surface is pinned in `tool-contract.json` so agent configurations are protected from silent renames.
contexts.name: mcp-server

contexts.api_surface: render(kind, value) -> Option<String> — dispatches by MCP tool name / CLI verb
contexts.description: Renders raw LightTrack API JSON responses for observability-domain endpoints into compact, human-readable Markdown for the `lt` CLI and `lt-mcp` server. Covers events, traces, scores, cost summaries, forecast reports, rollup tables, project listings, alert lists, label/calibration views, and collective-intelligence surfaces. Pure string work with no I/O: accepts a `serde_json::Value` and returns an `Option<String>` that callers fall back from to pretty-printed JSON on `None`. Depends on the shared `md` helper module and is held to `lighttrack-contract` by dispatch-table tests.
contexts.name: observability-rendering

contexts.api_surface: Implements Store trait methods: insert_score, list_scores_filtered, score_summary_by_dimension, create_benchmark, create_dataset, fork_dataset, import_dataset_items, create_rubric, insert_label, insert_calibration, create_prompt
contexts.description: Persists and queries the full evaluation stack: judge scores and their dimensional summaries, benchmark definitions and runs, eval datasets with fork/import lineage, scoring rubrics, human verdict labels, and judge calibration history. These tables form the quality ledger that gates prompt promotion and tracks model drift on managed Postgres deployments where production traffic flows.
contexts.name: pg-evaluation-store

contexts.api_surface: Implements Store trait methods: insert_event, insert_event_checked, list_events_filtered, rollup, list_traces, list_trace_events, redaction_posture
contexts.description: Persists and queries LLM call events, usage aggregates, rollups, distributed traces, and PII redaction posture against Postgres. The `events` module is split into write, list, filter, cost, and usage sub-files; `admission` gates duplicate events with a transaction-scoped advisory lock; `rollup` is the grouped-aggregate primitive that powers forecast and margin surfaces via trait defaults; `traces` groups spans into call trees.
contexts.name: pg-event-telemetry

contexts.api_surface: Implements Store trait methods: create_project, create_api_key, create_limit_rule, upsert_price, fill_unpriced_cost, insert_revenue_event, reprice_revenue, create_job, claim_job, create_schedule, create_relay_task, lease_relay_tasks, settle_relay_task, create_device, replace_collective_contribution, insert_alert_dedup, create_alert_channel
contexts.description: Implements the full set of platform plumbing surfaces on Postgres: project and API-key admin, usage limits, model pricing and revenue repricing, margin policies, background jobs with lease-fenced dequeues, cron schedules, cloud-to-device relay queue with concurrency-safe leases, device fleet registry, collective leaderboard with atomic contributor replacement, contribution ledger, and the alert ledger with dedup cooldown and routing channels. Also contains the crate root (`lib.rs`), shared SQL helpers (`util.rs`), Cargo manifest, and the conformance/metadata guard test suite.
contexts.name: pg-platform-operations

contexts.api_surface: Public API: scrub(text) -> ScrubResult, scrub_detailed(text) -> (String, ScrubReport), rule_set() -> Vec<PiiRule>, rules_fingerprint() -> &str
contexts.description: Heuristic PII anonymization library that is the regex pass of the dataset-building pipeline: it replaces structured PII (emails, IBANs, SSNs, secrets, card numbers, IPs, phone numbers) with typed placeholders before traces are stored for judge scoring. Rules run in a fixed precedence order (most-specific first) and are deliberately conservative to avoid mangling evidence the downstream judge will read. The rule set is exported as a versioned JSON fixture consumed by client SDKs so their `guard(no_pii)` checks stay in sync with the server scrubber; a SHA-256 fingerprint of the ordered rule set is stamped on every scrubbed row so rule-set drift is observable in the database.
contexts.name: pii-scrubbing

contexts.api_surface: generate, generate_chat, generate_deterministic, generate_http (library API)
contexts.description: Multi-provider candidate-output generation: routes `generate` / `generate_chat` / `generate_deterministic` calls to Anthropic (bare Messages API or `claude -p`), Google Gemini, OpenAI, and OpenRouter adapters. Enforces structured-output schemas with a schema-shed fallback, applies bounded exponential retry on transient failures (429/5xx/timeout), and stamps each outcome with determinism and schema-enforcement metadata. `http_target` supports operator-owned RAG/agent endpoints; `endpoint_probe` identifies what is answering at a re-pointed OpenAI-compatible base; `pool` and `retry` provide the shared HTTP client and backoff logic.
contexts.name: provider-generation

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/events, POST /v1/scores, GET /v1/limits/status, POST /v1/relay/tasks, GET /v1/relay/tasks/{id}
contexts.description: Python client library for ingesting LLM call telemetry to the LightTrack API from any Python application. The core `LightTrack` class sends events best-effort on a background daemon thread; `instrument`/`wrap` monkey-patch OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini SDK clients for zero-config auto-tracing with full trace/span context propagation via `contextvars`. Includes pre-spend admission control, crash-surviving span journals, PII detection, and output guard validation; ships with no third-party runtime dependencies.
contexts.name: python-sdk

contexts.api_surface: POST /webhook (LightTrack alert delivery), GET /health, GET /classification; consumes LightTrack GET /v1/events, GET /v1/scores, GET /v1/alerts, POST /v1/alerts/{id}/resolution; emits to Resend POST /emails
contexts.description: lt-responder is a local daemon that receives LightTrack alert webhooks (error spikes and quality regressions), classifies failures as transient vs code-side (using a carried `failure_class` field minted at the ingest boundary, with a phrase-list fallback), enriches each trigger with recent failing events or judge scores fetched from the LightTrack API, and runs a read-only Claude Code investigation against the locally-mapped repository. For opt-in projects it can also apply a gated auto-fix on a fresh `lt-fix/*` branch via an edit-mode Claude run, run the project's test command, and restore the original branch. Every run is bounded by a multi-layer circuit breaker (in-flight dedup, per-project cooldown, rolling-hour cap, concurrency semaphore) whose durable half is the LightTrack alert ledger so restarts don't reset the spend record. Finished diagnoses are persisted as Markdown files, posted back to LightTrack as alert resolutions, and optionally emailed via Resend.
contexts.name: reactive-alert-responder

contexts.api_surface: GET /v1/benchmarks/:id, POST /v1/benchmarks/:id/runs, GET /v1/prices, POST /v1/scores, POST /v1/calibrations
contexts.description: Runs stored benchmarks (compare mode, rubric mode, simple mode) and measures judge trustworthiness via Cohen's κ calibration against human-labeled datasets. Tracks per-run spend budgets with pre-flight cost guards and live ceilings, records case-level provenance and billing, and persists κ history for drift detection. Feeds benchmark run results and calibration scores back to the API for the Evaluation & Benchmarking UI.
contexts.name: runner-benchmark-calibration

contexts.api_surface: GET /v1/events, GET /v1/traces, POST /v1/scores, GET /v1/rubrics/:id
contexts.description: Executes LLM-as-judge scoring against stored events and traces: invokes the judge model, parses structured verdicts per rubric dimension, and posts scores back to the API. Handles single-event scoring, whole-trace sampling with settle windows, regression detection, batch judging (N cases per call), pairwise round-robin A-vs-B comparison, exec-dimension sandboxing, and CI gate exit codes. Depends on lighttrack-engine for the claude/provider driver and lighttrack-core for shared types.
contexts.name: runner-scoring-engine

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/jobs/claim, PATCH /v1/jobs/:id, GET /v1/jobs/:id, POST /v1/datasets, POST /v1/labels, POST /v1/billing/revenue
contexts.description: Provides the lt-runner binary's CLI surface, job-queue worker loop, and all data-pipeline commands: dataset build/import/fork, online sampling schedules, human label import, and Stripe billing sync. The serve loop claims jobs via leased poll, dispatches by JobKind, and renews heartbeats to survive transient API errors without a spurious takeover. Also owns the shared HTTP client, CLI argument structs, and utility helpers used across every other runner module.
contexts.name: runner-worker-pipeline

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/events, GET /v1/limits/status
contexts.description: Rust client library for ingesting LLM call telemetry into LightTrack from Rust applications. Reuses `lighttrack-core`'s `LlmEvent` as the wire type to prevent payload drift, sending events on a background thread via `reqwest`. Provides admission control, PII detection, and provider-response token extraction matching the shared SDK contract fixtures, packaged as a detached Cargo workspace so it builds and versions independently of the server.
contexts.name: rust-sdk

contexts.description: SQLite implementation of the Store trait's usage-governance surfaces: limit rule evaluation (atomic admission with per-project locking), margin policies, revenue events, price book operations, usage cache for rolling window queries, alert channels, and PII redaction stamps. The usage cache is critical-path infrastructure — it keeps rolling `usage_since` O(1) by incrementally maintaining a window aggregate rather than scanning the full event table.
contexts.name: sqlite-governance-backend

contexts.description: SQLite implementation of the Store trait's observability and scoring surfaces: event ingest/query, scores, score summaries, traces (via rollup), benchmarks, calibrations, rubrics, datasets, labels, prompts, and use-case registry. Each domain is a free-function module over a locked `&Connection`. Includes the SQLite unit-test suite covering concurrency, migrations, maintenance, metrics, and collective behaviour.
contexts.name: sqlite-observability-backend

contexts.description: SQLite implementation of the Store trait's platform-operations surfaces: projects, API-key management, background job queue (with lease renewal and cancellation), schedule records, database maintenance (WAL checkpoint, incremental vacuum), in-process metrics ring, relay task lifecycle, and device registry. The `pool.rs` and `mod.rs` modules wire up the single locked connection and implement `SqliteStore`. The `schema.rs` here applies the declarative schema to a live connection.
contexts.name: sqlite-platform-backend

contexts.api_surface: POST/GET /v1/jobs, POST /v1/jobs/:id/finish, POST/GET /v1/projects/:id/schedules, GET /v1/schedules, GET /v1/storage/status, GET /v1/projects/:id/redaction
contexts.description: Manages durable background work and store maintenance. The job queue supports claim/progress/finish/cancel lifecycle for async benchmark runners and other workloads; stored schedules drive recurring job kinds on a configured interval via a background sweep. The storage module implements quiet-window SQLite maintenance (checkpoint, WAL compaction) gated on an activity gauge, exposing disk accounting and the maintenance flight recorder via a status endpoint. Redaction posture is enforced here at the ingest boundary.
contexts.name: storage-and-jobs

contexts.description: Backend-agnostic conformance test harness for governance and platform-operations domains: admission control, pricing, revenue, margin policies, refusals, jobs, relays, devices, schedules, tenancy, and database maintenance. Ensures every backend implementation honours the Store trait's admission semantics, limit enforcement, and operational contracts. Paired with the observability conformance half; together they cover the full Store trait surface.
contexts.name: store-conformance-governance

contexts.description: Backend-agnostic conformance test harness for the observability and scoring domains: events, scores, traces, rollup, forecasting, labels, prompts, use-cases, dataset lineage, collective intelligence, contributions, and alerting. Each module exposes a parameterized test function that any backend runs against to prove Store-trait compliance for that surface. Depends on `conformance/fixtures.rs` for shared test data construction.
contexts.name: store-conformance-observability

contexts.description: Integration and property tests for the store crate that run outside the source tree: schema equivalence across backends, schema documentation generation, backend-parity assertions, a soak test for concurrent ingest, a timestamp-format guard, and a legacy migration fixture that proves the SQLite backend can upgrade a pre-M14 schema forward. These tests exercise the full store stack end-to-end and are the regression guard for migration correctness.
contexts.name: store-integration-tests

contexts.description: Declarative, backend-agnostic schema DSL that describes every LightTrack table, column, and migration step once, then renders SQL for SQLite, Postgres, BigQuery, and human-readable documentation. Tables are grouped into domain modules (ingest, eval, ops, registry) so adding a column touches one file. Consumed by every backend's `init_schema` and by the schema-equivalence test suite.
contexts.name: store-schema-definition

contexts.api_surface: Rust trait Store — consumed by crates/api, crates/mcp, crates/runner
contexts.description: Defines the backend-agnostic `Store` trait (~180 methods), all shared DTOs (EventFilter, TraceFilter, Usage, Admission, CostRow, etc.), and utility modules used by every backend. It is the single authoritative contract between the API layer and any persistence backend — SQLite, Postgres, or Firestore. Depends on `lighttrack-core` for domain types; consumed by `crates/api`, `crates/mcp`, and every store backend.
contexts.name: store-trait-and-types

contexts.api_surface: POST /v1/events, POST /v1/scores, GET /v1/limits/status, POST /v1/relay/tasks
contexts.description: TypeScript/JavaScript client library for ingesting LLM call telemetry to LightTrack from Node.js or browser applications. Mirrors the Python SDK's feature set — auto-instrumentation, admission control, crash-surviving journals, PII guard, relay task dispatch — using the global `fetch` API with zero runtime dependencies. Tests assert the shared SDK contract fixtures to prevent cross-language drift.
contexts.name: typescript-sdk

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/limits, POST /api/limits, GET /api/alerts
contexts.description: Provides the per-project usage limit evaluation engine: rules, scopes, thresholds, throttle/block escalation logic, and the alert and webhook-signature types that notify operators when limits are breached. The six integration tests in crates/core/tests guard repo invariants (manifest commands, blocking CI gates, guidance projections, chart policies) and are co-located here as the closest governance context.
contexts.name: usage-governance-limits
